slots.practicalActivity: Create a real project folder, run python -m venv .venv, activate it, install numpy, pandas, matplotlib, and jupyter with pip, freeze the exact versions into requirements.txt, then launch Jupyter and create a notebook with one markdown cell and one working code cell that imports all 4 packages successfully.
slots.deliverable: A working local virtual environment with a committed requirements.txt (pinned versions) and one Jupyter notebook that successfully imports numpy, pandas, and matplotlib and prints their versions.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a script with at least 6 variables representing a real small-retailer configuration (a list of 10 order totals, a discount threshold, a tax rate, a currency string, a boolean for free-shipping eligibility), then use if/elif/else to classify each of the 10 order totals as 'small', 'medium', or 'large' and loop over the list printing each classification.
slots.deliverable: One script with 6+ correctly-typed variables and if/elif/else logic that classifies and prints a small/medium/large label for each of 10 sample order totals.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a function apply_discount(total, rate) and a function total_with_tax(total, tax_rate) that compose correctly, then use a list comprehension to compute the final charged amount for a list of 10 raw order totals, and a dict comprehension to build an {order_id: final_amount} lookup from the same data.
slots.deliverable: Two working functions plus one list comprehension and one dict comprehension, run against 10 sample orders with printed final amounts.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a list of dicts representing 8 orders, each with order_id, customer_id, a list of item names, and a total, then write code that groups the orders into a dict keyed by customer_id (each value a list of that customer's orders), and use a set to find which customers bought at least one item in common.
slots.deliverable: One script that transforms a list of 8 order dicts into a customer_id-keyed grouping dict, plus a set-based check for customers sharing at least one purchased item.

slots.practicalActivity: Add 3 deliberately broken records to your order list (one with a missing price, one with a price as a string like 'N/A', one with a negative quantity), then wrap the processing loop in try/except blocks that catch ValueError and KeyError specifically (not a bare except) and print a clear message per bad record instead of crashing; use pdb.set_trace() or an IDE breakpoint to step through one bad record and confirm exactly where it fails.
slots.deliverable: One script that processes 8 good plus 3 broken order records without crashing, catching at least 2 distinct exception types by name, plus a written one-sentence note on what the debugger showed for one failure.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a NumPy array of 20 realistic order totals, then use boolean masking to apply a 10% discount only to orders over $100 in one vectorized operation (no loop), and use slicing to pull out every 3rd order and the bottom/top 5 by value.
slots.deliverable: One NumPy array with a vectorized, boolean-masked discount applied to orders over $100, plus a sliced view showing every 3rd order and the top/bottom 5 by total.

slots.practicalActivity: On the same 20-order NumPy array, compute the mean, median, standard deviation, and 25th/75th percentiles with NumPy, then build a second array of item counts per order and compute the Pearson correlation coefficient between order total and item count with np.corrcoef.
slots.deliverable: Printed mean/median/std/25th-75th percentile for the order-totals array, plus one correlation coefficient between order total and item count.

slots.practicalActivity: Using numpy.random.default_rng with a fixed seed, simulate 1000 days of order counts drawn from a distribution with a realistic average (around 40 orders/day with some spread), compute and print the simulated mean and standard deviation, then rerun with the same seed to confirm you get identical results.
slots.deliverable: One reproducible NumPy simulation (fixed seed) of 1000 daily order counts with printed mean/std, confirmed identical on a second run with the same seed.

slots.practicalActivity: NumPy practice lab: simulate 2000 draws of a second quantity (e.g. items-per-order) with a different distribution shape than the previous slot's, combine it with your order-totals array using broadcasting to compute a derived array (e.g. price-per-item), and report the mean/std/percentiles of the derived array.
slots.deliverable: One combined, broadcasted NumPy array (e.g. price-per-item across 1000+ simulated orders) with full summary statistics printed.

slots.practicalActivity: Download a real small retail or sales dataset (for example a public Kaggle sample like 'Superstore' or a similarly-sized free CSV), load it into a DataFrame with pd.read_csv, inspect it with .head(), .info(), and .describe(), and pull one numeric column out as a standalone Series to compute its .sum() and .mean() directly on the Series.
slots.deliverable: One DataFrame loaded from a real downloaded CSV with .head()/.info()/.describe() output, plus one Series extracted from it with its own .sum()/.mean() computed.

slots.practicalActivity: On the same dataset, use .loc and a boolean condition to select only rows matching a specific real criterion (e.g. orders above the median value, or from one region/category), then create 2 new columns: one computed from existing columns with simple arithmetic, and one computed with .apply() and a custom function.
slots.deliverable: One filtered subset of the real dataset (via .loc and a boolean condition) plus 2 new derived columns, one via arithmetic and one via .apply().

slots.practicalActivity: Sort the dataset by a numeric column to find the top 10 and bottom 10 rows, use .rank() to rank every row by that same column, and use .value_counts() on a categorical column to find the 5 most common categories.
slots.deliverable: A top-10/bottom-10 sorted table, a full .rank() column, and a .value_counts() breakdown of the 5 most common values in one categorical column.

slots.practicalActivity: Parse a date column with pd.to_datetime (handling at least one messy format if present), extract the year, month, and day-of-week into 3 new columns, and compute the number of days between that date and today using a timedelta.
slots.deliverable: One properly parsed datetime column, 3 derived date-part columns (year/month/weekday), and a days-since calculation shown for every row.

slots.practicalActivity: pandas Fundamentals practice lab: combine this chapter's skills on a second real dataset you have not used yet (filter it, add 2 derived columns, sort/rank it, and parse any date column it has), and write a one-paragraph summary of the single most interesting finding the filtering or ranking surfaced.
slots.deliverable: One cleaned, filtered, and ranked DataFrame from a second real dataset, with a written one-paragraph summary of a specific finding.

slots.practicalActivity: Group the dataset by a categorical column (e.g. product category or region) and use .agg() to compute the sum, mean, and count of a numeric column for each group in one call, then sort the result to find the single highest-performing group by total.
slots.deliverable: One grouped summary table with sum/mean/count computed together via .agg(), sorted to show the top-performing group.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a small lookup DataFrame (e.g. category_id to category_name) and merge it onto the main dataset with both an inner join and a left join, printing the row-count difference between the two; then build a pivot_table summarizing total sales by category and month, and use .melt() to convert that pivot table back into long format.
slots.deliverable: One merged DataFrame showing the inner-vs-left join row-count difference, plus a pivot table (category by month) and its melted long-format equivalent.

slots.practicalActivity: Compute a 7-period rolling average of a numeric column (e.g. daily sales) with .rolling(7).mean(), and separately clean a real text column using at least 3 string methods (.str.lower(), .str.strip(), .str.contains() or .str.replace()) to standardize messy category or product-name text.
slots.deliverable: One 7-period rolling-average column plus one text column cleaned with at least 3 chained .str methods.

slots.practicalActivity: pandas in Depth capstone lab: using groupby, merge, a pivot/reshape, and a rolling calculation together, answer one specific real question about your dataset (for example 'which category grew fastest month-over-month?' or 'which region's sales are most volatile week to week?'), and write a 2-3 sentence conclusion stating the answer with the actual numbers that support it.
slots.deliverable: One notebook or script combining groupby, merge, reshape, and a rolling/window calculation to answer a stated question, with a 2-3 sentence written conclusion citing real numbers.

slots.practicalActivity: Run .isna().sum() on the full dataset to locate every gap, decide and apply a fix per column (dropna with subset= where a gap is rare, a group-aware fillna with .transform('median') for a numeric column with a real pattern), then find and remove exact duplicate rows with .duplicated() and .drop_duplicates(), printing row counts before and after each step.
slots.deliverable: A full missing-data report, a documented fill-or-drop decision per affected column, and a before/after row count for duplicate removal.

slots.practicalActivity: Find a column stored as text that should be numeric (strip currency symbols/commas and convert with pd.to_numeric or .astype()), then flag outliers in a real numeric column using the IQR method (values below Q1-1.5*IQR or above Q3+1.5*IQR), counting how many rows get flagged.
slots.deliverable: One column successfully converted from messy text to numeric type, plus an IQR-based outlier flag column with a printed count of flagged rows.

slots.practicalActivity: Write at least 5 validation assertions against the cleaned dataset (no negative prices, no dates outside a plausible range, no order with zero items, all required columns present, no duplicate order IDs) and produce a pass/fail report naming which rule failed and how many rows violated it.
slots.deliverable: A validation script covering 5+ real rules, producing a pass/fail report naming violated rules and row counts for each.

slots.practicalActivity: Data Cleaning capstone lab: download a fresh, messier real dataset slice you haven't cleaned yet, and run a complete pipeline end to end: diagnose and handle missing values, remove duplicates, fix at least one data-type problem, flag outliers with the IQR method, and run your validation checks from the previous slot against it.
slots.deliverable: One end-to-end cleaning script run against a new real dataset, with a before/after summary of row count, column count, and validation pass/fail results.

slots.practicalActivity: Write your cleaned dataset out to CSV, Excel (.xlsx), and JSON with pandas, confirming each file opens correctly, then connect Python to a real SQL database (SQLite is fine if SQL Server isn't available) and use pd.read_sql with an actual SQL query (not just the whole table) to pull data into a DataFrame.
slots.deliverable: The same cleaned dataset successfully written to CSV, Excel, and JSON, plus one real SQL query result pulled into a DataFrame via pd.read_sql.

slots.practicalActivity: Call a free public REST API (for example a currency exchange-rate API or a public holiday API) with the requests library, inspect the raw JSON response, and parse the relevant fields into a DataFrame row or a Python dict you could join onto your retail dataset by date or currency.
slots.deliverable: One working REST API call with its JSON response parsed into usable Python data (dict or DataFrame row).

slots.practicalActivity: Pick one public webpage with a simple HTML table (checking its robots.txt first) and use requests plus BeautifulSoup to scrape that table into a DataFrame with at least 3 columns, printing the first 5 scraped rows.
slots.deliverable: One real scraped table loaded into a DataFrame with 3+ columns and its first 5 rows printed.

slots.practicalActivity: Files, Databases & APIs practice: build one enriched DataFrame that combines data from at least 2 different sources covered in this chapter (for example your file-based retail data joined to the API's exchange-rate or holiday data by date), handling any mismatched keys or formats between the sources.
slots.deliverable: One combined DataFrame merging data from at least 2 different source types (file, SQL, API, or scrape) from this chapter.

slots.practicalActivity: Take one of your messiest notebook cells from earlier in the course and refactor it into 2+ well-named functions following PEP8 (snake_case names, docstrings, no magic numbers), then move those functions into a standalone .py module and import and call them successfully from a notebook.
slots.deliverable: One refactored .py module with 2+ documented, PEP8-named functions, successfully imported and called from a notebook.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a pytest test file with at least 3 test cases for one real data function you built earlier (for example the outlier-flagging or discount function), including one normal case, one edge case (an empty list or a zero value), and one case that should raise an error, and run pytest to confirm all 3 pass.
slots.deliverable: One pytest file with 3+ passing test cases (including one edge case and one error case) for a real function from this course, confirmed by an actual pytest run.

slots.practicalActivity: Pin every package version in requirements.txt by re-running pip freeze, set and document every random seed used anywhere in your course scripts, and write a short README-style note listing the exact commands needed to recreate your environment and rerun your analysis from a clean clone.
slots.deliverable: A pinned requirements.txt, a written list of every seed value used in the course's scripts, and a short reproducibility README with the exact rerun steps.

lessons.title: Capstone Kickoff: Clean and Analyze a Real Dataset in Python

slots.practicalActivity: Choose one real public dataset you have not used elsewhere in this course, state 2-3 specific analysis questions you want it to answer, and load and inspect it with .head(), .info(), and .describe() to confirm it can actually answer them.
slots.deliverable: One chosen real dataset, 2-3 written analysis questions, and an initial .info()/.describe() inspection confirming the data can address them.

slots.practicalActivity: Execute the full capstone pipeline on your chosen dataset using techniques from across the whole course: clean missing data and duplicates, fix any data-type problems, engineer at least 2 new columns, and compute the specific aggregations or statistics needed to answer your 2-3 stated questions.
slots.deliverable: One complete analysis notebook/script that cleans the chosen dataset, engineers 2+ new columns, and produces the specific results answering all 2-3 stated capstone questions.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a one-to-two-page portfolio summary of your capstone project in plain language: state your original questions, your key numeric findings, one limitation of the data or method you used, and package the notebook/script and summary together as something you could show in a job interview.
slots.deliverable: A one-to-two-page written portfolio summary of the capstone project (questions, findings, one stated limitation) packaged alongside the finished notebook/script.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can set up a real Python environment, manipulate data with NumPy and pandas (filtering, grouping, merging, reshaping, cleaning), pull data from files, SQL databases, and APIs, and package that work into tested, reproducible scripts -- the working toolkit the rest of the Data Scientist path's statistics, visualization, and machine learning courses are built on.
